text:
OpsBot: :rotating_light: Pager — reserved pool 'resv-aurora-42' reports GPU saturation and queue growth for tenant PeregrineHealth. Severity: P1. Alert: >95% GPU util on all 8 reserved GPUs, queue length 11.8k, incoming request rate spike.
Maria (oncall): ack — taking.
Raj: assigning triage. main symptoms? errors or just latency?
Devon: both — 504s and timeouts showing up in customer logs, but most requests are stuck queued waiting for GPU allocation. autoscaler logs show repeated attempt to create nodes then failing with quota error: "quota_per_customer_exceeded".
Lee: confirming from infra — allocation API returned 403 quota limit for PeregrineHealth (reserved burst limit hit). Autoscaler retried x6, backoff applied.
Maria (oncall): estimated impact — PeregrineHealth webhooks failing, elevated 5xxs since ~1739485000, support ticket #CH-9127 opened. Sophie, do we have customer on the phone?
Sophie: yes, customer ops called 8m ago, they're seeing degraded inference for clinical routing. They've escalated to their SRE. They're asking for ETA.
Corey: support note: multiple clients behind PeregrineHealth report 504s. SLA at risk.
Raj: immediate mitigations: 1) evict noisy sessions in the reserved pool; 2) move lower-priority infer jobs to fallback hosted pool; 3) request temporary quota bump from quota service / cloud team. Which can we do now?
Devon: eviction script ready: `scripts/evict_noisy_sessions --pool resv-aurora-42 --threshold 75` — will drop sessions with sustained >75% GPU per session for last 1m. This should free ~2 GPUs worth based on recent telemetry.
Maria (oncall): run it and watch. tagging @Lee for cloud quota request.
Lee: running eviction now. command output: ```evict_noisy_sessions: scanned 124 sessions, evicted 19 sessions, freed ~1.9 GPUs equivalent```
OpsBot: automated note — eviction job completed (run by Maria).
Devon: routing policy change — switching PeregrineHealth low-priority traffic to hosted-fallback-1. Applying route: `route set --tenant PeregrineHealth --priority low --target hosted-fallback-1`
Maria (oncall): applied. Watch for increased latencies on fallback but should reduce queue.
Corey: adding customer message template — "We're rerouting non-critical requests to a fallback pool to reduce impact, core inference for critical paths remains prioritized."
Raj: cloud quota update?
Lee: on the quota request — cloud team responded: can approve temporary increase but needs 15-20m manual approval for compliance checks. Requested now, ETA ~18m.
Sophie: sharing update with customer: we have evicted noisy sessions and started routing lower-priority traffic to fallback; requesting quota bump in progress, will update in 20m.
Devon: autoscaler logs show repeated 429/insufficient capacity errors from provisioning provider for shared burst nodes — likely a regional shortage. Fallback routing is essential.
Maria (oncall): symptoms trending — queue dropping from 11.8k -> 7k after eviction/reroute, 5xx rate decreasing but still elevated.
OpsBot: Incident timeline note created.
Raj: longer-term: need to enforce tenant-level slot caps and better preemptive shedding to prevent a single tenant from saturating reserved pool. Create a follow-up action item.
Sophie: customer on call wants to escalate to account exec if SLA breach occurs. Logging that.
Lee: cloud approval just came through — temporary quota bump +2 GPU-equivalent nodes granted. Spinning up now.
Devon: new nodes provisioned and attached to pool, but healthchecks show a few warmup failures; retrying.
Maria (oncall): monitoring — queue now 2.1k, GPU util trending down to ~70%. 5xxs down to baseline+1.
Corey: sending status update to PeregrineHealth: "We've freed GPU capacity by evicting noisy sessions and routing low-priority traffic to a fallback pool. Additional capacity provisioned; monitoring continues."
Raj: are we confident the noisy tenant was the root cause? What if this recurs?
Devon: telemetry points to a misbehaving job from one of PeregrineHealth subtenants that opened many long-running sessions (model fine-tuning loop accidentally hitting inference endpoints). We'll need to correlate session IDs with customer-side job IDs.
Maria (oncall): handoff plan — I'll stay on for 30m, then pass to night oncall (Lee) with notes: eviction run, routing change, quota bump granted, queue baseline 2k and falling.
Lee: ack — I'll pick up at 1739490000.
Sophie: coordinating customer follow-up and postmortem request.
OpsBot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Please file postmortem with action items: tenant caps, autoscaler fallback improvements, preemptive quota checks.
Maria (oncall): filing quick postmortem draft. Adding action items and owners.
Devon: adding logs & session IDs to doc for correlation.
Corey: closing customer-facing update thread after Sophie posts details.
Sophie: will schedule a follow-up call with PeregrineHealth for 0900 tomorrow to review impact and remediation.
Maria (oncall): handing off now — leaving detailed notes in incident doc. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
Lee: taking over. monitoring alerts suppressed for noisy eviction noise for next 30m.
OpsBot: Incident closed (status: handoff to oncall).
